artists.biography: Bob Stanley is a British musician, journalist, author, and film producer. He is a member of the indie pop group Saint Etienne and has had a parallel career as a music journalist and author, writing for NME, Melody Maker, Mojo, The Guardian and The Times, as well as writing several books on music and football. His second publication, Yeah! Yeah! Yeah!: The Story of Modern Pop, was published by Faber & Faber in 2013. His third publication Let's Do It: The Birth of Pop Music: A History was published by Pegasus in 2022. He also has a career as a DJ and as a producer of record labels, and has collaborated on a series of films about London.

artists.biography: Pete Wiggs (born15 May 1966, Reigate, England) is an English musician, producer, songwriter and DJ, best known for being one third of Saint Etienne. Since the mid-2000's, he has completed a sizeable amount of remixes for other artists, mostly using Saint Etienne as an alias but also under his own name. In December 2014, his first official solo recording effort was released - Saint Etienne Presents How We Used to Live, a soundtrack for the documentary film of the same name. His second solo release was in April 2018 and was the soundtrack to the short film Abstractions of Holderness, made by Saint Etienne bandmate, Bob Stanley. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
The Tears Of Technology, compiled by Bob Stanley and Pete Wiggs and released in 2020 on Ace Records, is a definitive collection of early 1980s British synthpop and electronic music. The album showcases the emotional and melodic potential of synthesizers during a pivotal era, highlighting tracks from both well-known pioneers like John Foxx and the Human League, as well as lesser-known acts such as Turquoise Days and Electronic Circus. The compilation captures the period between 1978 and 1984, when affordable synths and post-punk experimentation allowed a new wave of artists to explore electronic melancholia, synthesized intimacy, and innovative pop songwriting.

Musically, the album emphasizes the genre’s shift from the synth as a novelty or threat to an instrument capable of deep emotion and melodic beauty. Stanley and Wiggs, best known as members of Saint Etienne, bring their curatorial expertise to this project, reflecting their longstanding interest in British pop history and electronic music. The compilation is praised for its thoughtful selection and historical context, with critics noting its celebration of a brief but influential era when synth-driven duos and bands reshaped the UK pop landscape. Upon its release, The Tears Of Technology received strong critical acclaim for its insight into the genre’s evolution and its role in preserving the legacy of early electronic pop.
